name: Maths
description: Try algebra, percentages, Pythagoras, indices and circle geometry.

questions.prompt: Simplify 2x + 3x.
options: 5x
5x²
6x
6x²
questions.explanation: Both terms contain x, so add their coefficients: 2 + 3 = 5. The result is 5x.

questions.prompt: What is 20% of 80?
questions.explanation: 20% is one fifth. One fifth of 80 is 16.
Expand to get 10x − 15 = 3x + 13. Subtract 3x and add 15 to get 7x = 28, so x = 4.

questions.prompt: A right-angled triangle has a hypotenuse of 13 cm and one shorter side of 5 cm. Find the other shorter side.
options: 8 cm
18 cm
12 cm
questions.explanation: For the missing shorter side, a² = 13² − 5² = 169 − 25 = 144. Taking the positive square root gives 12 cm.

questions.prompt: Simplify (27x⁶)^(2/3), where x > 0. The notation ^(2/3) means raised to the power two-thirds.
options: 9x²
18x⁴
3x⁴
9x⁴
questions.explanation: Apply the power to both factors: 27^(2/3) = (∛27)² = 3² = 9, and (x⁶)^(2/3) = x^(6 × 2/3) = x⁴. The result is 9x⁴.

questions.prompt: A circle has centre O and radius 10 cm. A chord AB is 12 cm long. Find the area of triangle AOB.
options: 48 cm²
60 cm²
96 cm²
24 cm²
questions.explanation: The perpendicular from O bisects the chord, so each half is 6 cm. Pythagoras gives the perpendicular height as √(10² − 6²) = 8 cm. The triangle’s area is ½ × 12 × 8 = 48 cm².

name: Applications of Maths
description: Explore everyday money, data, measures and practical calculations.

questions.prompt: You want to compare the number of pupils who chose each of four different lunch options. Which display is most suitable?
options: A scatter graph
A line graph showing a journey
A bar chart
A map with contour lines
questions.explanation: A bar chart compares frequencies in separate categories, such as lunch choices.

questions.prompt: Four journey times are 10, 15, 20 and 25 minutes. What is the mean journey time?
options: 15 minutes
17.5 minutes
20 minutes
70 minutes
questions.explanation: The total is 70 minutes. Divide by 4 to get a mean of 17.5 minutes.

questions.prompt: A jacket costs £80. It is reduced by 15%. What is the sale price?
questions.explanation: 15% of £80 is £12. Subtract that discount from £80 to get £68.

questions.prompt: Rice costs £2.40 for 600 g, or £3.60 for 1 kg. Which pack has the lower price per kilogram?
options: The 600 g pack
They cost the same per kilogram
There is not enough information
The 1 kg pack
questions.explanation: The 600 g pack costs £4 per kilogram. The 1 kg pack costs £3.60 per kilogram, so it is better value.

questions.prompt: £2,250 is invested at 3% compound interest per year. No money is added or withdrawn. What is the balance after two years, to the nearest penny?
questions.explanation: Multiply by 1.03 for each year: £2,250 × 1.03² = £2,387.025. Round the final balance to £2,387.03.

questions.prompt: Minibus A costs £60 plus £0.40 per kilometre. Minibus B costs £95 plus £0.25 per kilometre. For a 180 km trip, which is cheaper, and by how much?
options: B by £8
A by £35
They cost the same
A by £8

name: English
description: Read a short passage and explore language, evidence and analysis.

questions.prompt: Read: ‘Maya paused outside the classroom, took a slow breath, and finally pushed open the door.’ Which interpretation is best supported?
options: Maya may feel nervous about entering
Maya is looking for a lost book
Maya has already finished the lesson
Maya is certain nobody is inside
questions.explanation: Pausing and taking a slow breath suggest hesitation or nerves. The passage does not establish the other details.

questions.prompt: ‘The wind whispered through the empty streets.’ Which technique is most clearly used?
options: A statistic
Personification
A rhetorical question
A list
questions.explanation: The wind is given the human action of whispering. This is personification.

questions.prompt: Read: “Although the hall was crowded, Isla felt marooned.” What does “marooned” most clearly suggest in this context?
options: She is enjoying the crowd’s attention
She is travelling across the sea
She feels isolated despite being surrounded by people
She cannot remember where the hall is
questions.explanation: “Marooned” suggests being stranded and alone. The contrast with the crowded hall conveys emotional isolation rather than a literal journey.

questions.prompt: Read: “Around her, everyone celebrated. She counted the minutes.” Which analysis best explains the contrast?
options: The sentences show that everyone shares the same feelings
The sentences list the stages of a celebration in detail
The short second sentence proves she is late
The short second sentence focuses on her discomfort, contrasting with the happiness around her
questions.explanation: The first sentence establishes celebration. The short, focused second sentence shifts to her preoccupation with time, suggesting a different experience.

questions.prompt: A paragraph argues that galleries should offer free entry. The next begins: “Access is only the beginning. Without continued investment, a free gallery soon becomes an empty promise.” How does this link the ideas?
options: “Access” refers back to free entry, while “only the beginning” introduces the need for ongoing funding
It abandons the issue of access and begins an unrelated description
It argues that charging admission is the only possible solution
It repeats the first paragraph without adding a new consideration
questions.explanation: “Access” connects with free entry in the previous paragraph. “Only the beginning” signals a move to another requirement: continued investment.

questions.prompt: Read: “Libraries must adapt, not disappear. Digital learning tools matter, but so do shelves of books and quiet places to think.” Which conclusion best brings together the writer’s argument?
options: Libraries should remove books to make room only for computers
Libraries should combine digital resources with reading and study spaces
Libraries should avoid all technological change
Quiet study spaces make every other library service unnecessary
questions.explanation: The writer supports adaptation while retaining existing strengths. The best conclusion combines digital provision with books and quiet spaces, rather than selecting only one element.

name: Physics
description: Check foundations in motion, forces, circuits, waves and energy.

questions.prompt: An object travels 200 m in 10 s. What is its average speed?
options: 2 m/s
20 m/s
questions.explanation: Speed = distance ÷ time = 200 ÷ 10 = 20 m/s.

questions.prompt: In a simple series circuit with no branches, how does the current compare at different points?
options: It is the same at every point
It is used up by the first component
It must be zero after a resistor
It increases each time it passes a bulb
questions.explanation: In a series circuit, the same current flows through every component. Current is not used up.

questions.prompt: A resultant force acts on a 5 kg object, producing an acceleration of 2 m/s². What is the force?
options: 3 N
7 N
questions.explanation: Use F = ma: 5 × 2 = 10 N.

questions.prompt: A sound wave travels at 340 m/s and has a frequency of 680 Hz. What is its wavelength?
options: 2 m
questions.explanation: Rearrange v = fλ to λ = v ÷ f. The wavelength is 340 ÷ 680 = 0.5 m.

questions.prompt: A 12 V supply is connected to 4 Ω and 2 Ω resistors in series. What power is dissipated in the 4 Ω resistor?
options: 8 W
questions.explanation: Total resistance is 6 Ω, so I = V/R = 12/6 = 2 A. For the 4 Ω resistor, P = I²R = 2² × 4 = 16 W.

questions.prompt: A 0.50 kg object falls from rest through 4.0 m. Ignore air resistance and use g = 10 m/s². What is its speed just before it reaches the ground, to one decimal place?
questions.explanation: Gravitational energy lost is mgh = 0.50 × 10 × 4.0 = 20 J. Set ½mv² = 20: 0.25v² = 20, so v = √80 = 8.9 m/s to one decimal place.

name: Chemistry
description: Explore particles, bonding, acids and chemical reactions.

questions.prompt: An atom has 6 protons. What is its atomic number?
options: It depends on its number of neutrons
questions.explanation: Atomic number is the number of protons in the atom. Here it is 6.

questions.prompt: A solution has a pH of 3. How is it classified?
options: Neutral
Alkaline
Acidic
Always harmless
questions.explanation: A pH below 7 is acidic. pH alone does not establish whether a substance is safe to handle.

questions.prompt: An atom has atomic number 12 and mass number 25. How many neutrons does it have?
questions.explanation: Mass number is protons plus neutrons. The atom has 12 protons, so it has 25 − 12 = 13 neutrons.

questions.prompt: Which equation correctly balances hydrogen reacting with oxygen to form water?
options: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O
H₂ + O₂ → H₂O
H₂ + 2O₂ → H₂O
2H₂ + 2O₂ → H₂O
questions.explanation: Both sides have 4 hydrogen atoms and 2 oxygen atoms in 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O.

questions.prompt: Magnesium reacts with excess hydrochloric acid: Mg + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂. If 2.4 g of Mg reacts completely, what mass of hydrogen forms? Use relative formula masses Mg = 24 and H₂ = 2.
questions.explanation: There are 2.4/24 = 0.10 mol of Mg. The equation gives 1 mol H₂ for each mol Mg, so 0.10 mol H₂ forms. Its mass is 0.10 × 2 = 0.20 g.

questions.prompt: 20 cm³ of 0.50 mol/l sodium hydroxide exactly neutralises 25 cm³ of hydrochloric acid. The reaction is HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H₂O. What is the acid concentration?
options: 0.04 mol/l
0.25 mol/l
0.40 mol/l
0.625 mol/l
questions.explanation: Convert volumes to litres. Moles of NaOH = 0.020 × 0.50 = 0.010 mol. The 1:1 ratio means 0.010 mol HCl in 0.025 l, so its concentration is 0.010/0.025 = 0.40 mol/l.

name: Biology
description: Try cell structures, photosynthesis, enzymes and living systems.

questions.prompt: In a typical animal cell, which structure contains most of its genetic material?
options: Cell membrane
Cytoplasm
Nucleus
Cell wall
questions.explanation: The nucleus contains most of the cell’s DNA. Animal cells do not have cell walls.

questions.prompt: Which structure in a green leaf cell absorbs light for photosynthesis?
options: Cell wall
Nucleus
Vacuole
Chloroplast
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll, which absorbs light energy for photosynthesis.

questions.prompt: Increasing light intensity increases a plant’s oxygen production from 10 to 18 bubbles per minute. Further increases in light leave it at 18. What is the best explanation?
options: The plant has stopped photosynthesising entirely
Light can never affect photosynthesis
Another factor may now be limiting the rate
The result proves carbon dioxide is present in unlimited amounts
questions.explanation: The initial rise suggests light was limiting. The plateau suggests another factor, such as carbon dioxide availability or temperature, may now limit the rate.

questions.prompt: Why can a very high temperature stop an enzyme from working effectively?
options: It changes every substrate into water
It always makes the enzyme larger
It can change the shape of the enzyme’s active site
It removes all particles from the solution
questions.explanation: High temperatures can denature an enzyme, changing the active site so the substrate no longer fits effectively.

questions.prompt: In a monohybrid cross, both parents have genotype Bb. B is dominant and b is recessive. Out of 120 offspring, approximately how many would be expected to show the recessive phenotype?
questions.explanation: The cross Bb × Bb gives BB, Bb, Bb and bb. One quarter are expected to be bb and show the recessive phenotype: 120 × ¼ = 30.

questions.prompt: Two potato strips each start at 10.0 g. After equal times, the strip in a dilute solution is 11.2 g and the strip in a concentrated solution is 9.1 g. Which statement correctly describes the results?
options: The dilute-solution strip gained 12% mass; the concentrated-solution strip lost 9% mass
Both strips gained water because both were in solutions
The dilute-solution strip gained 1.2% mass; the other lost 0.9%
The concentrated-solution strip gained 9% mass; the other lost 12%
questions.explanation: Percentage change uses the starting mass: 1.2/10 × 100 = 12% gained, and 0.9/10 × 100 = 9% lost. The pattern is consistent with water entering or leaving cells by osmosis.

name: History
description: Practise evidence, chronology, causes and historical interpretation.

questions.prompt: Which is a primary source for investigating a soldier’s experience in 1916?
options: The soldier’s diary written in 1916
A school textbook published in 2020
A modern film set during the war
A summary written by a historian in 2010
questions.explanation: A diary produced by the soldier at the time is primary evidence for their experience. It still needs critical evaluation.

questions.prompt: Which sequence puts these years in order from earliest to latest?
questions.explanation: For these AD/CE dates, the smaller year comes first: 1914, then 1918, then 1939.

questions.prompt: In a practice source, a factory owner’s public statement claims their factory has excellent working conditions. Why does its purpose matter when evaluating usefulness?
options: A source with a persuasive purpose can provide no historical evidence
The owner may emphasise positives, so its claims should be checked against other evidence
A public statement is automatically an independent inspection
A statement’s purpose is unrelated to how it presents conditions
questions.explanation: The owner may want to protect the factory’s reputation. That affects how claims are presented, while the source can still be useful evidence of the owner’s position.

questions.prompt: In a practice example, an inspector records accidents at one factory, while a worker from that factory describes long hours. What is the strongest supported use of these sources together?
options: They prove conditions were identical in every factory
They cancel one another out because they discuss different details
They remove the need to consider who produced either source
They provide evidence about different aspects of that factory, with limits on wider generalisation
questions.explanation: The accounts address different aspects of conditions at the same factory. They may contribute to a wider argument, but do not alone establish conditions everywhere.

questions.prompt: In a practice scenario, a reform follows a long campaign and a sudden economic crisis. Evidence shows the campaign shaped the proposal before the crisis. Which judgement best uses this evidence?
options: The campaign helped shape the reform, while the crisis may have accelerated its adoption
The crisis must have created every idea in the proposal
The campaign cannot have mattered because the reform came later
The evidence proves only one factor could have influenced the reform
questions.explanation: The timing supports a role for the campaign in shaping the proposal. The later crisis may also have influenced adoption; a developed explanation weighs their different contributions.

questions.prompt: A campaigner publishes a leaflet during an event and gives an interview about it 30 years later. The two accounts agree. What is the strongest evaluation?
options: They are independent proof because they use different formats
Their agreement shows consistency, but their shared author limits independent corroboration
The later account must be more accurate simply because it is newer
The leaflet has no value because the author later discussed the event
questions.explanation: Both accounts come from the same person. Their consistency is relevant, but they are not independent corroboration; purpose, memory and other sources also need consideration.

name: Geography
description: Explore map skills, weather data and human–environment links.

questions.prompt: A six-figure grid reference contains how many digits?
options: Two
Four
Six
Eight
questions.explanation: A six-figure grid reference uses three digits for the easting and three for the northing.

questions.prompt: Which statement describes climate rather than a single weather event?
options: It is raining this afternoon
A strong gust occurred at noon
The temperature fell last night
The region usually has mild, wet winters over many years
questions.explanation: Climate describes long-term patterns and averages. Weather describes shorter-term atmospheric conditions.

questions.prompt: On a map with a scale of 1:50,000, two places are 4.6 cm apart in a straight line. What is their actual straight-line distance?
options: 23 km
2.3 km
230 km
questions.explanation: At 1:50,000, 1 cm represents 50,000 cm = 0.5 km. Therefore 4.6 × 0.5 = 2.3 km.

questions.prompt: A district has a population of 12,000 and an area of 30 km². What is its population density?
options: 360,000 people/km²
40 people/km²
2,500 people/km²
400 people/km²
questions.explanation: Population density = population ÷ area = 12,000 ÷ 30 = 400 people per km².

questions.prompt: A river is 2.0 m wide, with a mean depth of 0.40 m and a mean velocity of 0.75 m/s. Use discharge = cross-sectional area × mean velocity. What is its discharge?
questions.explanation: Using width × mean depth, cross-sectional area is 2.0 × 0.40 = 0.80 m². Discharge is 0.80 × 0.75 = 0.60 m³/s.

questions.prompt: Two similar catchments receive the same intense storm. Forested catchment A has higher annual rainfall, but built-up catchment B has the higher peak river flow. Which explanation best fits?
options: Higher annual rainfall must always produce the higher peak flow in an individual storm
Impermeable surfaces in B can reduce infiltration and speed runoff; annual totals alone do not explain the storm response
Built-up surfaces absorb every drop of water before it reaches a river
The peak flows prove that the two catchments received different storms
questions.explanation: Impermeable surfaces can send water to rivers more quickly. An annual rainfall total does not by itself explain a catchment’s response to one particular storm.

name: Modern Studies
description: Check ideas about democracy, evidence, inequality and rights.

questions.prompt: What is a key feature of a representative democracy?
options: Voters elect people to make decisions on their behalf
Only one person may express an opinion
Elections never take place
Public representatives cannot be questioned
questions.explanation: In a representative democracy, elected representatives make decisions on behalf of voters and can be held accountable.

questions.prompt: How many Members of the Scottish Parliament are there?
questions.explanation: The Scottish Parliament has 129 MSPs: 73 constituency MSPs and 56 regional MSPs.

questions.prompt: In a survey of 600 adults, 270 support a proposal. What percentage of those surveyed support it?
questions.explanation: 270 ÷ 600 × 100 = 45%. This describes the sample; it does not automatically establish the views of all adults.

questions.prompt: A council evaluates a service using an optional survey answered only by its current users. What is an important limitation?
options: Current users cannot have any useful views
An optional survey always has a 100% response rate
The survey automatically includes everyone who could not access the service
The sample may exclude non-users facing access barriers and may overrepresent those motivated to respond
questions.explanation: Current users can provide useful information, but an optional user survey may miss people unable to access the service and may be affected by self-selection.

questions.prompt: Unemployment falls from 35% to 28% among programme participants, and from 20% to 17% in a comparison group. The groups were not randomly selected or closely matched. What is the strongest conclusion?
options: Both rates fell and the participant fall was larger, but group differences limit a claim that the programme caused the change
The programme is proven to have caused every participant to find work
A fall of seven percentage points means unemployment fell by 7% of its original value
The comparison group’s fall means the programme cannot have helped anyone
questions.explanation: The falls are seven and three percentage points. The larger participant fall is relevant, but the different groups and other influences prevent a firm causal conclusion from these figures alone.

questions.prompt: Evidence suggests rural patients face long travel distances, while urban patients face long appointment waits. Which recommendation responds most fully to both findings?
options: Provide only more urban parking spaces
Explore rural outreach or transport alongside measures to improve urban appointment access
Assume the same single barrier affects every patient
Remove rural services because urban areas have more patients
questions.explanation: The recommendation addresses the distinct barriers identified in each setting. It still needs evaluation of feasibility, cost and likely impact.

name: Business Management
description: Explore stakeholders, costs, customer needs and business choices.

questions.prompt: Which description best defines a stakeholder?
options: Only the person who designed a logo
A product held in a warehouse
A person or group with an interest in a business
Any item bought in a shop
questions.explanation: Stakeholders have an interest in a business. They can include owners, employees, customers and suppliers.

questions.prompt: A business earns revenue of £1,000 and has total costs of £700. What is its profit?
questions.explanation: Profit = revenue − total costs, so £1,000 − £700 = £300.

questions.prompt: A product sells for £15. Its variable cost is £9 per unit and total fixed costs are £600. How many units must be sold to break even?
questions.explanation: Contribution per unit is £15 − £9 = £6. Break-even output is £600 ÷ £6 = 100 units.

questions.prompt: A business asks only members of its loyalty scheme about demand for a new product. Why should it be cautious when predicting demand among all potential customers?
options: Existing customers can never provide useful feedback
The sample may be more engaged with the business than non-members
A loyalty scheme guarantees a random sample of the whole market
Research removes all uncertainty about future demand
questions.explanation: Loyalty members can be useful respondents, but they may not represent people who are not already engaged with the business.

questions.prompt: Making a product costs £900 in fixed costs plus £4 per unit. Buying it costs £7 per unit with no fixed cost. For 400 units, which option costs less, and by how much?
options: Buying costs £300 less
Making costs £300 less
Making costs £900 less
Buying costs £1,200 less
questions.explanation: Making costs £900 + 400 × £4 = £2,500. Buying costs 400 × £7 = £2,800. Making is cheaper by £300 at this output.

questions.prompt: Opening cash is £1,800. This month, cash receipts are £1,600, operating payments are £2,200 and equipment costs £500. A further £900 of credit sales will not be paid until next month. What is closing cash this month?
questions.explanation: Closing cash is £1,800 + £1,600 − £2,200 − £500 = £700. The £900 credit sales are not a cash receipt this month.

name: Psychology
description: Try research methods, variables, ethics and interpreting results.

questions.prompt: In an experiment, what is the independent variable?
options: The variable the researcher deliberately changes
The result that is measured
Every characteristic of every participant
A conclusion written after the study
questions.explanation: The independent variable is manipulated to investigate its effect on the dependent variable.

questions.prompt: A study changes the length of a word list and measures how many words people recall. What is the dependent variable?
options: The length of the list
The number of words recalled
The title of the study
The researcher’s name
questions.explanation: The number recalled is the measured outcome, so it is the dependent variable.

questions.prompt: Students who report more revision time tend to have higher test scores. This is an observational correlation. Which conclusion is justified?
options: Extra revision is proven to be the only cause of higher scores
Every student who revises longer will get the same score
Revision time and scores are associated, but other factors may also contribute
The data show there is no relationship between the variables
questions.explanation: An association is present, but motivation, prior knowledge and other variables could contribute. Correlation alone does not establish causation.

questions.prompt: A participant agreed to take part in a study but now wants to stop. Which response best respects their right to withdraw?
options: Require completion because consent can never be changed
Threaten a penalty for leaving
Tell them their decision is irrelevant to the study
Allow them to stop and explain what will happen to their data under the agreed procedure
questions.explanation: Consent is ongoing. Participants should be able to withdraw without pressure, with information about the agreed handling of their data.

questions.prompt: A memory study gives caffeine to a morning group and no caffeine to an evening group. The morning group performs better. Which change most directly addresses the confounding variable?
options: Test both conditions at a comparable time and randomly allocate participants, keeping other procedures consistent
Keep the different times and only change the questionnaire colour
Give caffeine to everyone and remove the comparison condition
Assume time of day cannot affect memory
questions.explanation: Caffeine condition is confounded with time of day. Comparable testing times, random allocation and consistent procedures help isolate the effect being investigated.

questions.prompt: A study with 12 people per group reports mean recall scores of 18 and 16. It gives no information about variation or statistical testing. Which conclusion is most justified?
options: The difference is definitely statistically significant
One group recalled two more items on average, but the summary alone does not establish statistical significance
Every person in the first group outperformed every person in the second
The sample means prove a result that applies to the whole population
questions.explanation: The means describe the two groups, but do not show the spread of scores or whether the difference is likely to reflect more than chance variation.

name: Media
description: Explore audience, representation, language and media purpose.

questions.prompt: What is a target audience?
options: Only the people who made a media text
Every person who has ever watched television
The group a media text is especially intended to reach
The equipment used to record sound
questions.explanation: A target audience is the intended group. Their interests and characteristics can influence media choices.

questions.prompt: In media analysis, what does representation refer to?
options: Only the price of a camera
Only the number of actors
The length of a recording cable
How people, places or ideas are portrayed
questions.explanation: Representation concerns the way people, places and ideas are constructed and presented in media texts.

questions.prompt: A character is filmed from a low angle, brightly lit, with triumphant music. Which interpretation best connects these choices?
options: They necessarily show the character is frightened and weak
They give a neutral numerical account of the character’s height
They can work together to present the character as powerful or heroic
They prove every viewer will admire the character
questions.explanation: Low angle, lighting and music can combine to construct a heroic or powerful image. Audience responses can still vary.

questions.prompt: A social-media post uses a popular creator, a discount code and a direct link to buy a product. Which analysis best explains these choices?
options: The code proves the post has no commercial purpose
The creator’s popularity makes the post independent of advertising
A purchase link means the audience’s interests do not matter
The post uses the creator’s appeal and an incentive to encourage purchases from a target audience
questions.explanation: The creator, discount and buying link work together as persuasive commercial choices aimed at an audience.

questions.prompt: Two posters advertise the same running club. A shows a lone runner at sunrise with “Beat yesterday”. B shows a smiling group with “Make Sundays social”. Which comparison is best supported?
options: A emphasises personal challenge, while B emphasises belonging; these are different appeals rather than proof of who will actually join
Both posters can appeal only to professional athletes
The different pictures mean the club must offer different sports
B contains no persuasive choices because it shows a group
questions.explanation: The images and slogans suggest personal improvement in A and social connection in B. Analysis can identify intended appeals without assuming a uniform audience response.

questions.prompt: A report on a protest repeatedly shows broken windows and interviews only business owners. It omits footage of peaceful marching and comments from organisers. Which analysis is strongest?
options: The choices prove all protesters damaged property
Selection of images and voices can frame the event around disruption and business concerns, limiting other perspectives
The report must be a complete account because it contains interviews
Only the length of the report affects its representation
questions.explanation: Repeated images and selected interviewees can foreground disruption and business concerns. Omitting other footage and voices narrows the perspectives represented.
